title: Find the perimeter of a region bounded by arcs of two intersecting circles
content: When two circles intersect at two points and a shaded region is bounded by an arc from each circle, first find the coordinates (or key length) of an intersection point by solving the two circle equations simultaneously. Then, for each circle in turn, find the angle subtended at that circle's own centre by the two intersection points, using right-angle trigonometry (e.g. cosine of half the angle = horizontal distance from centre to intersection point, divided by the radius) or the cosine rule in the triangle formed by the centre and the two intersection points. Decide, from the diagram, whether the arc that borders the shaded region corresponds to that angle or to its reflex counterpart (2*pi minus the angle), then compute each arc length using s = r*theta with the correct angle, and add the two arc lengths together to get the perimeter.
